title: Bekasi Marathon 2026: A Flat, Tree-Lined Loop That Tests Your Heat Tolerance
meta_description: An honest look at Bekasi Marathon 2026 in Kota Harapan Indah — flat, shaded course, strict cut-offs, hot August conditions, and tricky transport access.
dek: Now in its fifth edition, Bekasi Marathon trades big-city spectacle for a steady, cone-lined loop through a Bekasi township — flat and green, but hot, strict on time, and a genuine mission to reach without a car.
verdict: Bekasi Marathon suits runners who want a straightforward, well-marshalled flat course to chase a PB or simply finish comfortably inside generous-but-firm cut-offs. The tree-lined loops through Kota Harapan Indah keep things visually pleasant and the water stations frequent, but the August date brings real heat risk on an exposed route, and reaching the venue without private transport is a hassle. It's a solid, community-flavoured regional race rather than a bucket-list event — good for locals, PB hunters comfortable with heat, and anyone happy to Grab or drive in.

sections.heading: The Course: Flat, Shaded, and Traffic-Free
paragraphs: Bekasi Marathon's route stays entirely within and around the Kota Harapan Indah township, weaving through residential streets and shophouse rows rather than heading out onto highways or industrial roads [3]. One runner reviewing the course described it as fairly sterile and cone-separated, with plenty of roadside trees as the route loops through housing, shophouses, and the surrounding Harapan Indah area [3].

For the Full Marathon specifically, past-edition coverage describes the layout as reasonably flat and lined with shady trees, which is a meaningful plus given Bekasi's reputation for heat [4]. Race organisers themselves lean into the township setting, framing Kota Harapan Indah as a green, comfortable environment built to support runners' performance [5].

Because the course loops repeatedly through a contained residential-commercial pocket rather than pushing into open exposed terrain, it should feel more like a big training loop than a scenic point-to-point — comparable, per one runner's shorthand, to the vibe of running around a BSD-style township [3].

sections.heading: Conditions: August Heat is the Real Opponent
paragraphs: The date shift matters. The 2025 edition ran in February and was hit by rain at the start, but runners note that August in Bekasi typically means hot conditions instead [3]. With the 2026 edition flag-off scheduled for early morning — 04:00 WIB for the Full Marathon, 05:00 for the Half, 05:45 for the 10K, and 06:00 for the 5K — organisers have clearly built in some buffer before the sun gets fierce [2].

Even so, a flat, tree-lined course only offsets so much heat once the morning wears on, and the shift from a rainy February race to a hot August one changes the calculus for pacing and hydration planning considerably [3][4].

sections.heading: Organisation and Logistics: Good on Course, Tricky to Reach
paragraphs: On-course support gets solid marks: one participant review rates water stations as reliably placed roughly every 2.5 kilometres, calling the aid-station coverage safe and dependable [3]. The 2025 recap similarly points to organisers deploying trained medical teams and marshals to help participants finish comfortably and safely.

Getting to the start line is the bigger sticking point. The venue sits well outside easy public-transport reach — the nearest train station, Kranji, is about 9km away, and the local TransJakarta route only serves the return trip rather than the outbound journey to the venue, according to one runner's account [3]. Anyone without a car or motorbike should plan carefully, likely via ride-hailing, well ahead of a 4am flag-off.

Cut-off times are strict and are explicitly built into the race's identity. The Full Marathon cut-off sits at 6 hours, Half Marathon at 3 hours 30 minutes, 10K at 2 hours, and 5K at 1 hour 30 minutes [2][5]. The 2025 race director framed hitting those cut-offs, whatever the conditions, as a point of pride tied directly to the event's #TaklukkanBekasi ('Conquer Bekasi') slogan.

sections.heading: Atmosphere and Field Size
paragraphs: Bekasi Marathon draws a respectable regional field rather than a mass-participation crowd — the 2025 edition brought together 2,025 participants from various regions, a nice round-number milestone organisers highlighted in their recap. The event bills itself as more than a race: a celebration of the local running community, with runners chasing everything from a simple finish to a personal best [5].

The 2026 edition markets itself as volume five of the series, continuing the same #TaklukkanBekasi spirit and inviting runners to enjoy the tidy, green feel of the Kota Harapan Indah township while testing themselves against the clock [6]. Perks for entrants include a race jersey, bib, finisher medal, and sponsor products, according to the event listing [2][7].

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you're based in or near Bekasi and want a flat, shaded course to test fitness without traveling far, this is a sensible regional pick — the terrain is forgiving and aid stations are frequent [3][4]. It's less appealing as a destination race for out-of-towners, given the venue's distance from train stations and the outbound gap in TransJakarta service, so factor in a car, motorbike, or ride-hailing budget [3].

Runners chasing a comfortable time cushion should note the cut-offs are firm rather than generous for a hot-weather race, and the August date raises the heat stakes compared with the rain-soaked 2025 edition [2][3]. Overall, it's a well-marshalled, community-oriented event best suited to those who prioritise a flat course and don't mind sorting their own transport.
Registration for the 2026 edition covers 5K, 10K, Half Marathon, and Full Marathon distances, with race-pack collection listed for early August ahead of the 9 August 2026 event date [1][2].

faqs.question: When is Bekasi Marathon 2026 and where is it held?
faqs.answer: Bekasi Marathon 2026 takes place on Sunday, 9 August 2026, in the Kota Harapan Indah area of Bekasi, Jawa Barat, offering 5K, 10K, Half Marathon, and Full Marathon distances [1][2].

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times for Bekasi Marathon 2026?
faqs.answer: Cut-offs are 6 hours for the Full Marathon (04:00 WIB flag-off), 3 hours 30 minutes for the Half Marathon (05:00 WIB), 2 hours for the 10K (05:45 WIB), and 1 hour 30 minutes for the 5K (06:00 WIB) [2].

faqs.question: Is the Bekasi Marathon course flat?
faqs.answer: Yes — reviewers describe the Full Marathon route as fairly flat and lined with shady trees as it loops through the Kota Harapan Indah residential and shophouse area, cone-separated from traffic [3][4].

faqs.question: How do I get to the Bekasi Marathon venue without a car?
faqs.answer: It's not straightforward: the nearest train station, Kranji, is about 9km away, and the local TransJakarta route only covers the return trip, not the trip out to the venue, per a runner's account [3].
